body:
`insight:nifty-eps-vs-index-returns` | confidence: verified | date: 2026-11-19

Long run, Indian index returns track earnings growth plus dividends plus valuation change. Data points: Marcellus estimates Nifty 50 EPS grew ~10% CAGR over FY05-FY25, with an unusual 24% CAGR over FY21-24 (post-Covid, bank/NBFC cleanup, commodity margins) slowing to ~6% in FY25; Business Standard (May 2025) reported Q4FY25 Nifty EPS growth of just 4.7%, slowest since 2017, and index EPS rising from Rs503 (Mar-2021) to ~Rs1,071. Price return Jun-2005 to Jun-2025: Nifty 2,220.6 to 25,517, ~12.98% CAGR (BacktestIndia) - i.e., ~2-3 points a year of P/E expansion on top of ~10% EPS growth (our arithmetic; NSE also switched from standalone to consolidated earnings for P/E in 2021, which complicates the P/E series). Nifty 50 TR since Nov-1995 is 12.15% (NSE factsheet, 30 Oct 2026); Finnovate computes that by FY26 the 20-year rolling Nifty CAGR dropped below 10% for only the second time, and from the Jan-2008 peak the CAGR to end-FY26 was ~7.3%. Trailing P/E ~19.3-20.7 in Oct 2026 vs ~23-24 a year earlier. Lessons: (1) budget 10-12% nominal index returns, not 15%; (2) starting from high P/Es (2008, 2021, 2024) produced subpar multi-year returns - the same valuation-return link Marks shows for the S&P; (3) earnings growth bursts (2003-08, 2021-24) do the heavy lifting. Actionable: decompose any stock's expected return into EPS growth + dividend yield + P/E change, and refuse theses that need P/E expansion from already-high levels.

Sources:
- https://marcellus.in/newsletter/consistent-compounders/earnings-growth-in-india-sliding-nifty-rising-ccp/
- https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/nifty-50-eps-grew-just-4-7-in-march-quarter-slowest-pace-since-2017-125051301530_1.html
- https://backtestindia.com/data/nifty-50-cagr
- https://www.finnovate.in/learn/blog/nifty-20-year-cagr-below-10-percent-history
- https://www.niftyindices.com/Factsheet/ind_nifty50.pdf
- https://siblisresearch.com/data/cape-ratio-india-nifty/

Forward, dated, probabilistic predictions about measurable events, used to **test methods** (lessons L11, L15).
They are **not recommendations** — no call says or implies buy/sell. Each is scored with Brier score against
a naive base-rate forecaster when it resolves (Jan–Jun 2027). Seed file: `memdb/seeds/2026-11-21_paper_calls_batch1.json`.

Context noted across Q2 FY27 / Q3 CY26 calls (Oct–Nov 2026): RBI in a tightening cycle (repo hiked to 5.5%, more hikes
expected), El Niño/drought stress in parts of India, high crude and 'exceptional' input-cost inflation, West Asia supply-chain
disruption, transmission-line delays for renewables. These shape several sector-cycle calls.

Margin convention for India calls: unless the rule says 'company-reported', margins are computed as Operating Profit ÷ Sales
from screener.in's quarterly table (consolidated unless marked standalone), to one decimal.

**Count:** 35 calls — india: 20, us: 15. By method: promise-tracker: 12, sector-cycle: 6, base-rate: 6, mgmt-tone: 6, flags-judgment: 3, valuation-temperature: 2.

- NSE only; BSE-only companies need `tools/bse_fetch.py` (HTTP/2).
- Segment numbers are not covered: add a results-PDF/XBRL parser that writes the `--csv` format.
- Data access is fragile: NSE and screener change hosts, headers and markup without notice.
  Re-run `financials.py SYMBOL` and `fetch.py` each quarter as a smoke test.
- Precision tuning: candidates are deliberately high-recall. If the LLM budget on the Pi is tight,
  use `--min-tier A`, which loses about 15 points of recall.

body:
| | SKIPPER | UNIPARTS |
|---|---|---|
| Manual promises the scorer accepts (coverage) | 20/68 (29%) | 23/68 (34%) |
| **Numbers only, both resolved: exact agreement** | **8/11** | **14/14** |
| Same, using the LLM-structured version of each promise | 5/7 | 11/11 |
| After the chain rule, both resolved: exact / direction | 7/12 / 10/12 | 14/14 / 14/14 |
| LLM path after the chain rule: exact | 9/16 | 12/13 |
| Moved goalposts, manual / auto / both | 9 / 12 / 5 | 6 / 2 / 2 |

**The disagreements are boundary cases, not arithmetic errors:**
- SKIPPER "below 4.5%" finance cost: actual 4.63%. The pilot called it missed; the late rule gives
  partly because the next quarter's TTM figure met it.
- ">25% in FY25 and FY26": the pilot gave partly as a composite of the two years; the scorer
  only checks FY26, so it says missed.
- The FY26 "25% plus" revenue chain: the pilot said missed; the chain rule says moved-goalpost
  because the guidance was relabelled "aspirational" and cut without being acknowledged. Arguably the
  stricter reading is correct, but it is a judgment call. The rule pushes SKIPPER's hybrid MCS from
  −0.18 to −0.34.
- UNIPARTS goalposts missed by inference: the Mexico storyline sits under different metric names and
  categories. LLM `chain_key`s fix this partly. The pilot's "H2 > H1 / Q4 highest" shape promise is
  not auto-scorable.

**Coverage is about 30%, not the ~60% the pilot hoped for.** The gap is promises that are financial
but not on screener: segment revenue (polymer, aftermarket, infra), order inflow and order book,
capex, and company-defined working-capital days. The next step is to parse the quarterly results
PDFs (`nse_fetch.py results`) for segment data and feed them in as `--csv`.
